sources.title: Renewables 2025
sources.excerpt: The report examines renewable deployment through 2030 across electricity, transport and heat, together with policy and market conditions.

sources.title: Energy Storage
sources.excerpt: Storage can retain wind and solar energy for periods when those resources are unavailable. The page describes batteries and pumped storage hydropower.

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: Renewable deployment is shaped by policy and market conditions. The IEA’s Renewables 2025 examines electricity, transport and heat through 2030. [1] Storage gives variable wind and solar generation a way to serve demand at other times. The US Department of Energy describes both battery research and pumped storage hydropower. [2]
bullets: Review the policy assumptions behind an outlook.
Keep source evidence attached to the briefing.

sections.title: Market landscape
sections.text: The IEA considers policy changes, manufacturing trends and the financial health of renewable industries. Its outlook spans multiple energy uses rather than electricity alone. [1]

sections.title: Storage and flexibility
sections.text: The Department of Energy describes storage as a response to intermittent wind and solar supply. Pumped storage uses reservoirs at different elevations and generates power as water moves through a turbine. [2]
bullets: Batteries retain energy for later use.
Pumped storage uses water and elevation.

sections.title: Risks and considerations
sections.text: A forecast depends on its assumptions. The IEA’s report assesses sector challenges as well as opportunities. [1] For this briefing, leadership should examine local conditions before applying a global outlook.
bullets: Separate a forecast from an observed result.
Review local policy and project constraints.

sections.title: Next steps
sections.text: Use the linked sources to check scope and context. This sample recommends reviewing policy assumptions and assessing storage needs before developing a project-specific plan.
